rationale: Both come from the one iMessage attachments setting: F001 is the config flip that lets a photo or PDF reach the agent and F002 is what the model then does with it, so neither has a result without the other. Same wave A, same medium risk, same agents (each parent's own), and the local privacy gate F084 stays a separate card because Tony can still decide whether attachments go on before that gate exists.
name: Inbound photos and PDFs: attachments reach Happy and are understood

rationale: These four are what standing up the research agent consists of: the agent entry with search and fetch, the gateway egress settings that keep it off the home network (WEB-01 lists F019 as its dependency), and the citation, freshness and fact-check rules written into its instructions (F025's rubric is described as folded into the F022 section). All are low risk, config and prompt text only, and sit on the one memory-less agent, so no riskier half or trifecta boundary is hidden; F025's later wave reflects priority, not a dependency.
name: Stateless research agent: public web reading behind egress guardrails, with cited, dated and fact-checked answers

rationale: F064 is the same explain-this prompt program on the parent's own agent with a five-line template for insurance statements and medical bills in place of the general one; both need only attachments switched on and no new tool. F064's later wave has no dependency behind it, and the merged card must say that claim details reach the cloud model and carries F064's medium risk, so the more sensitive half is not hidden.
name: Explain this: document, school message, medical bill or EOB, homework concept or how-to

rationale: The reply-language directive is rendered into the same per-person USER.md, by the same generator, from the same family file and under the same character cap as the other standing preferences. Both are wave A, ready now, need no tool and add no send path; the merged card keeps F042's medium risk.
name: Family facts, standing preferences and reply language rendered into each parent's agent from the family file

rationale: F032's capture is the F030 Reminders tools themselves (adding an item to a shared list), plus one scheduled Saturday list job per parent, so the pair is one plugin and one job on the same agents. Same medium risk and no new recipient or data source; the bridge keeps its wave A place and the card notes that the Saturday job is switched on with the other scheduled texts.
name: Shared Reminders lists: add and tick off by text or voice, plus a Saturday shop list

rationale: All three are one change to the family generator and the scheduler settings: the registry emits each job from the family file, the charters are rendered from those same entries, and the guardrails are the time limit and tool cap put on every job the registry emits plus the scheduler's failure-alert and missed-run settings. Both additions list the registry as their dependency, all are wave A, low risk and operator-only, and none grants an agent anything.
name: Jobs registry with per-feature flags, a written charter per job and unattended-job guardrails

rationale: The lock-out phrase is specified as an extension of the kill-switch plugin and shares its dispatch hook, so both are built and tested as one in-house plugin. Both are wave A and low risk, both can only narrow what Happy does, and switching things back on stays with the operator in each case.
name: Stop phrases: the 'stop everything' kill switch and locking one person out after a lost phone

rationale: Both are scheduled, read-only, host-side command jobs that text only the operator when something is broken or has changed, and OCL-13 names the health watch's delivery path as the one it reuses. Same wave A and low risk, no agent gains a tool, and the spend line (G004) stays separate because it carries its own hard-limit decision.
name: Operator self-checks: daily integration health and a change-based security audit

rationale: Both are entries in the one gateway-wide node command deny list, written before any Mac or phone is paired, so they are a single config change reviewed once. Both are wave A, low risk, ready now and purely restrictive, so nothing riskier is folded in.
name: Node command ceiling: deny computer control and phone commands first, then pair

rationale: Both decide when a proactive text may go out and keep their state in the same household store: the notification plugin's send checks for quiet hours and caps, and a paused-until window for mute and vacation, whose 'urgent alerts still arrive' lines up with G001's priority classes. Same wave B and low risk, and neither adds a recipient or a data source.
name: Notification policy: quiet hours, daily cap, priority classes, and snooze or vacation mode by chat

rationale: All three are the same job pattern: an isolated scheduled run per parent on that parent's own agent, capped to the weather tool and the read-only calendar and announced only to the owner, differing in the cron line and the prompt. Same wave B and medium risk, none of them reads mail, and which brief is switched on is a per-person flag in the jobs registry, not a separate build decision.
name: Scheduled calendar-and-weather briefs: evening logistics, weekday morning and Sunday week-ahead

rationale: All five run on the one school mailbox and its isolated school-mail reader: the mailbox and sender allowlist, the urgent one-line relay, the 16:00 digest job, and the per-platform and Classroom setup steps that only decide what lands in that mailbox. All are wave B and stay inside the same memory-less agent that can only announce to the two parents; the card carries SRC-08's medium risk and must say that grade and attendance emails reach the cloud model, while allowlist changes by chat (G016) and the parents' own inboxes stay separate cards.
name: School mailbox with isolated reader: urgent relay, 16:00 digest and per-platform feed setup

rationale: Both put outside schedules into the family calendar by subscribing a feed link that the read-only calendar then serves, and SRC-09's record says it gives G012 its real data sources, adding a no-model script for change alerts. Both are low risk and no agent fetches or parses a feed link (the calendar subscription and a host script do that), and G012's 'later' has no dependency behind it, so the whole ships with SRC-09 in wave B.
name: External calendar feeds (district, teams, library) with change alerts for sports schedules

rationale: F039 is specified as the same automation primitives as F038 over the same household-store rows, with a parent marking items done in both. Same wave B and low risk, and both are parent-run (the kids are not users), so nothing riskier is hidden.
name: Household schedules with nudges: upkeep, car care, bins and the kids' chore rota (parent-run)

rationale: All three are one job pattern: dated facts kept in the family's own config (the renewals table, a dates file, the pet facts) and a scheduled run on the parent's own agent that sends a short heads-up, differing in the table and the lead time. Same wave B, nothing is renewed, bought or ordered in any of them, and the merged card keeps the medium risk of F063 and F012.
name: Dates to remember: renewals and expiries, birthdays and gift dates, pet care

rationale: All three are the same operator-created command job with no model: fetch a public government recall list, keep seen ids in a state file, match locally against the family's own items and print one templated line or stay silent. All are low risk and no request carries more than a date range or a car's make, model and year; SRC-05's wave C has no dependency behind it, so the set ships together in wave B.
name: Recall watch matched to what the family owns: products (CPSC), food and medicine (FDA), vehicles (NHTSA)

rationale: Both are prompt-only templates on the parent's own agent that produce a text for someone outside the family, and both rest on the same limit: Happy sends nothing and the parent forwards it from their own phone. Same wave B, ready now with no build; the merged card keeps F036's medium risk because the sitter sheet draws on the children's facts.
name: Ready-to-forward texts for people outside the family: sitter or grandparent sheet, vendor, coach and carpool drafts

rationale: Both are the gateway's one speech-output block: F004 is the on-request audio reply with the built-in macOS voice, and VOX-04 swaps in a local neural engine and switches the online speech fallback off. VOX-04 lists F004 as its dependency, both are low risk on the same agents, and F004 has no wave of its own, so the whole ships in VOX-04's wave C.
name: Spoken replies with a local voice (online speech switched off)

rationale: F027 is the family-facing use of the F021 Places wrapper: the same host-side Places server on the research agent answers both 'is it open now' and 'three open-now picks nearby'. Same wave C, same low risk, same agent, and neither makes a reservation or a booking.
name: Places lookup and errand picks: open now, rating, phone and a Maps link

rationale: WEB-03 is the fail-closed hook that limits which profile, sites and actions the F020 research browser may use, and its record says the browser tool is all-or-nothing without it, so it has no value alone and the browser should not ship without it. Both are wave C on the research agent; the merged card states the reader and the firewall as two parts and carries WEB-03's medium risk.
name: Research browser and long-content reader, behind a browser action firewall

rationale: The mail agent, its read-only Gmail server and the lookup are one build: one agent entry per adult, one read-only account grant, and the first question it answers; the agent has no use without the tool and the tool has no holder without the agent. All are wave C at medium risk and read-only; draft writing (F048, F053), email-to-self (F049) and the morning digest stay separate cards, so the write half is not hidden.
name: Per-person mail agent with read-only Gmail and 'did I get an email about X?' lookup

rationale: F053 is the family-facing use of the F048 drafts server: the same write-drafts-but-never-send grant on the same adult's mailbox, with sending blocked by the same hook. Same wave C and medium risk; it is kept apart from the read-only mail card so that the write half stays visible.
name: Reply drafts in the owner's Gmail Drafts (Happy never sends)

rationale: F060 and F061 are both specified as the F050 watch with a different sender list: the same bundled mail-watch plugin, app-password grant and tool-less per-message reader on an adult's own Gmail, and F050 has no wave of its own. All are medium risk on the same person's inbox; the card must state the sender classes separately (health senders subject-only, payroll and bank senders arrival-only with contents never opened), and the school mailbox stays a separate card.
name: Trusted-sender watch on a personal Gmail: appointment, refill and travel-change emails, and a tax-form arrival checklist

rationale: CRT-12 names the F067 health-form helper as the part that supplies its copy-paste answers, and both rest on per-child facts kept in the family's private notes; F067 has no wave of its own. Same medium risk and the same parent's agent, and in both the parent fills, signs and submits, so the whole ships in CRT-12's wave C.
name: Enrolment, camp and health-form paperwork kit

rationale: Hue and Sonos are two command-line wrappers inside the same stateless home agent with the same local-network permission, HOM-02 is the decision record that selects exactly those two bundled tools, and the goodnight check is a no-model job that reads both. All are wave C; the card states the read-only check and the switching parts separately and carries high risk, while the Shortcuts bridge and Home Assistant stay separate cards.
name: Home agent for lights and speakers: Hue rooms and scenes, Sonos playback, and a goodnight check

rationale: HOM-11's buildable route is an allowlisted 'TV off' Shortcut run by the F078 plugin, and its record says the TV is the only HomeKit accessory in the house, so it is that plugin's first and only current use. Both are wave C and high risk with exact-name allowlists; the on-screen notice needs Home Assistant and is noted as a later part.
name: Allowlisted macOS Shortcuts bridge, first use: TV off at bedtime

rationale: HOM-14 describes itself as adding one thing to F080: the Sunday fridge sheet, which F080's name already includes, printed by a plain script through the same printer queue. Both are wave C; the card states the on-request print tool and the no-model scheduled sheet as two parts and carries F080's high risk.
name: Print it: PDFs, photos and pages to the home printer, plus a no-model Sunday fridge sheet

rationale: Both are the same act: installing the OpenClaw iPhone app and pairing it, which always creates a node session and an operator chat session together, and both records limit the first step to Tony's phone. Both are wave D; the card states the device-command surface and the chat surface as two parts and carries IPH-01's high risk, while Talk mode stays a separate card.
name: OpenClaw iPhone app on Tony's phone: pairing, device-command ceiling and a second chat surface

rationale: VOX-03 is the set of pairing scopes, Talk owner setting and speech-provider switches that has to be in place before any voice surface is switched on, and Talk mode is the only live voice surface placed in a build wave, so the guardrails have no value alone. Both are wave D; the card carries VOX-01's high risk, and realtime voice, the Watch and room devices stay separate later cards.
name: Talk mode on Tony's iPhone, with the voice guardrails pack

rationale: Both rest on the same grant and the same missing guard: self-paced automations created from a parent's own agent, which need a delivery pin on the automations tool, triggers switched off and the same command-owner decision. Both are medium risk on the same agent, and AUT-03 has no dependency beyond those shared ones, so the pair ships in AUT-01's wave D.
name: Self-paced automations on a parent's agent: multi-day project check-ins and watch loops

rationale: Both add another read-only Google service to a parent's own agent through the same gog tool and per-person sign-in, differing in which service is consented. Both are 'later', medium risk and read-only on that person's own account, so one card covers the grant.
name: More read-only Google data per person: Sheets, Docs, Drive and Contacts

rationale: MKT-13's chat hours and parent alerts are specified as living inside the kid-safety plugin already planned for F072, and the nightly digest is the other half of the parent oversight that has to exist when the kid agent first answers a child. All three are blocked on the same things (a local model and the children's own accounts), none can ship alone, and the card carries medium risk.
name: Kids agent base with parent oversight: safety classifiers, chat hours, parent alerts and a nightly digest

rationale: Both are prompt programs in the kid agent's own instructions (hint-first homework help and scored practice rounds) with no tool, blocked on the same kid agent and local model. Both are low risk and 'later'; the parent-run photo quiz (MKT-02) stays separate because it runs today on a parent's cloud-backed agent.
name: Kids' learning help: homework hints, curiosity answers and practice drills

rationale: These six are one screen-control pilot whose parts depend on each other: the Mac app node, the clean virtual machine it runs in, the one stateless agent allowed to hold the computer tool, the human view, the acceptance test and the single pilot task, none of which does anything alone. All are 'later' and five of the six are experimental, the card carries high risk, and the wave A default-deny stays a separate card.
name: Screen-control pilot: Mac app node in a clean VM, a stateless desk agent, a human view, an acceptance test and one pilot task (flat PDF form)

rationale: Both answer 'what does the porch look like' or 'did the package come' with one still picture, by a network camera or by a spare iPhone on a stand, and IPH-02 is written as an extension of F079. Both are 'later' and wait on hardware and on the same decision about where a camera is acceptable; the card states both routes and carries IPH-02's high risk.
name: Porch camera snapshot on request (network camera or a spare iPhone)

rationale: Both give the same answer to 'can Happy manage the kids' devices': no, because approvals live in the vendor's own parent app, with MKT-11 covering Apple Screen Time and CRT-07 covering the rest by its own description. Both are 'never' at high risk for the same reason (approving a child's purchase or download is on the never list), so one card hides nothing.
name: Managing the kids' devices (Screen Time, Chromebook, tablet, console): not through Happy
